correctness.rationale: The parameter-uniform incidence Gram eigenvalue identity is recovered from the subspace-lattice harmonic decomposition, and the distance-power matrix is expressed exactly as a combination of these two Gram operators, the identity, and the all-ones matrix. The degree-two eigenvalue is strictly largest on the mean-zero space for all positive exponents; it is strictly increasing from -1 to a positive value at exponent one. A unique sharp root and its kernel and asymptotic follow by elementary inequalities and Taylor expansion. Independently assembled exact binary incidence matrices and threshold computations corroborate the normalization. In particular, at \(q=2,n=6\) the direct incidence spectrum is verified via integer polynomial identities for matrices of sizes 63 and 651, not approximate eigenvalue fitting; enumeration of all dimensions is not asserted.

value.rationale: The generalized-roundness threshold is the exact boundary for Hilbert snowflake embeddings of the natural finite-field Grassmann graph metric. A unique degree-two harmonic obstruction is found across every q,n, and a new exponential-in-n collapse contrasts sharply with ordinary subset Johnson metrics. This structural, infinite-family phenomenon goes beyond a one-instance spectral exercise and motivates quantitative embeddings for subspace-code geometries.
